title: Envoy Gateway 1.9.1 Tightens Security and Addresses a Difficult Upgrade Path
gist: Envoy Gateway 1.9.1 reverses the v1.9.0 zero-second SDS/RDS fetch timeout that could leave proxies without TLS certificates during upgrades, and adds security fixes (CVE-2026-47775 AES-GCM cookies, no Wasm HTTP fallback, tenant security-context hardening) plus per-phase translation tracing.

insights.claim: Envoy Gateway 1.9.0 set the initial fetch timeout for Secret Discovery Service (SDS) and Route Discovery Service (RDS) to zero, which let a cluster wait indefinitely on a missing Secret or endpoint, stay in a warming state, block CDS updates and delay health checks.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Shows how a single default change in a gateway control plane can stall traffic config; audit timeout defaults before adopting minor releases.

insights.claim: Envoy Gateway 1.9.1 restores Envoy's default 15-second initial fetch timeout for SDS and RDS, returning to the v1.8.x behaviour.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: The fix is a rollback of the 1.9.0 change, so 1.8.x users face no regression.

insights.claim: Changing the SDS configuration while upgrading the Envoy Gateway controller can trigger an Envoy issue in which still-running proxies activate TLS listeners without certificates, so new TLS handshakes fail; backend TLS and the global rate-limit service can see similar certificate or CA problems.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Upgrading from v1.9.0 carries real outage risk for TLS ingress.

insights.claim: Envoy Gateway recommends v1.8.x users upgrade straight to v1.9.1 and skip v1.9.0, while v1.9.0 users should use a rolling-update setup that replaces proxy pods quickly, which needs spare cluster capacity and can interrupt long-lived WebSocket and gRPC connections.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Plan capacity and connection-drain tolerance before upgrading from v1.9.0.

insights.claim: A production user reported a GitHub issue in which long-running Envoy proxies lost their downstream TLS certificates and stopped serving HTTPS, and recovery needed manual proxy restarts; the issue tied it to new SDS subscriptions and the v1.9.0 timeout change.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Real-world evidence that the regression caused production outages.
insights.locator: A GitHub issue from a user

insights.claim: Envoy Gateway now uses AES-256-GCM for OAuth2/OIDC session-cookie encryption and drops the legacy AES-256-CBC decryption path to fix the padding-oracle vulnerability CVE-2026-47775; existing sessions will force users to re-authenticate after upgrade.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Expect a one-time re-login event on upgrade; deployments with a replacement Envoy bootstrap must configure runtime settings explicitly.

insights.claim: Envoy Gateway previously could fall back from HTTPS to plain HTTP when pulling OCI Wasm images from a registry that rejected HTTPS, which could let an on-path attacker supply arbitrary Wasm code; 1.9.1 removes the implicit fallback and allows HTTP only for registries explicitly configured as insecure.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: A supply-chain risk in extension loading is closed; check for registries relying on the old fallback.
insights.quote: Previously, an OCI registry that rejected an HTTPS request could cause Envoy Gateway to fall back to plain HTTP

insights.claim: A tenant-supplied EnvoyProxy configuration could fully replace Envoy Gateway's hardened Kubernetes security-context defaults, potentially allowing privileged execution or running as root; this is fixed in 1.9.1.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Multi-tenant gateway setups face a privilege-escalation boundary issue that is now patched.

insights.claim: Envoy Gateway 1.9.1 adds extra validation of OIDC issuer URLs and scopes OIDC flow cookies to the redirect path, which reduces propagation of abandoned authentication cookies.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi

insights.claim: Envoy Gateway now automatically watches namespace label changes so route acceptance is re-evaluated without a controller restart, and 1.9.1 also fixes hostname-conflict handling, controller crashes with missing optional CRDs, and consistent hashing for UDP routes.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Reduces operational toil and crash risk in dynamic multi-namespace clusters.

insights.claim: The global rate-limit integration now discovers replicas through Kubernetes Service and EndpointSlice data via EDS, keeping DNS resolution as a fallback, so requests keep reaching rate-limit replicas as they scale.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Better scaling behaviour for rate limiting.
insights.locator: The release also improves the global rate-limit

insights.claim: Envoy Gateway now emits per-phase tracing spans for Gateway API and xDS translation, covering listener processing, HTTP and gRPC routes, policy processing, EnvoyPatchPolicy handling, extension hooks and xDS validation, so slow translations can be pinpointed.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Useful for platform teams debugging control-plane latency at scale.

insights.claim: The author argues that running a Kubernetes-native gateway at scale means config changes can affect live proxy state, security boundaries extend into Wasm and tenant-controlled resources, and control-plane performance needs its own telemetry.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Gateway selection and operation should weigh upgrade safety, multi-tenancy isolation and control-plane telemetry.
insights.quote: configuration changes can affect live proxy state, security boundaries extend into Wasm and tenant-controlled resources
